channel.title: Crypto Docket
channel.description: Crypto Docket reports news across crypto: Bitcoin and Ethereum, layer-2 networks, DeFi, stablecoins, exchanges, regulation and security incidents.

item.title: Judge keeps Gemini’s $5 million CFTC settlement in place
item.description: Judge Alvin Hellerstein rejected Gemini and the CFTC’s joint bid to undo the 2025 order, leaving its injunction in place after the $5 million was paid.

item.title: Bridge Upgrades Are Coordination Problems Across Chains
item.description: Bridge gateway upgrades touch contracts, validators and applications at different speeds; staged releases reduce disruption but leave teams managing compatibility windows.

item.title: Why a Cross-Chain Bridge Can Wait on a Public RPC
item.description: A bridge can be ready while a public RPC is not; see why endpoint lag stalls cross-chain updates, how it differs from a failed transfer, and what to check next.

item.title: Route Simulation Shows the Likely Result Before You Sign
item.description: Route simulation tests a proposed transaction against a snapshot of chain state, showing likely token changes, gas use and failure points before you authorize it.

item.title: When Chain Maintenance Delays a Bridge, Check These Four Things
item.description: When chain maintenance slows a bridge, trace the source transaction, bridge status, destination claim and recovery terms before waiting, retrying or switching routes.

item.title: When Does a Bridge Actually Deliver Wrapped Tokens?
item.description: A bridge delivers wrapped tokens only after the source transfer is confirmed, its message is verified, and a destination transaction mints or releases the asset.

item.title: How to Check a Pending Mantle Token Migration
item.description: A pending BIT-to-MNT migration is a review request, not a bridge transfer. Check its status, compare transaction records and know when to wait or investigate.

item.title: A Wrong-Chain Transfer Is Not Always Lost
item.description: A wrong-chain transfer may be recoverable when you control the address on both networks; otherwise, recovery depends on the recipient or platform.

item.title: When a Route Stays Pending After Delivery
item.description: A route can remain pending after destination delivery because user settlement and treasury reimbursement are separate; reconcile each leg before retrying.

item.title: Moving Crypto Proceeds Into a Payment App Means Choosing an Off-Ramp
item.description: Moving crypto proceeds into a payment app usually means converting them to cash first; the best route depends on network support, fees, timing and how you plan to spend.

item.title: A dropped transaction can stop a cross-chain swap before it starts
item.description: A dropped source-chain transaction can leave a swap unstarted; after confirmation, cross-chain execution adds observation and payout stages, so timing depends on both chains.

item.title: Cross-Chain Swap Slippage: Set a Limit That Fits the Route
item.description: Set slippage against the quote and route, not a universal percentage: a wider limit can help a swap execute, but it accepts a worse final output.

item.title: A fairer way to compare cross-chain swap quotes
item.description: A fair cross-chain swap comparison starts with the same wallet-side amount and ends with assets actually spendable, after fees, timing and failure risk, before choosing a route.

item.title: Why a Monero–Bitcoin atomic swap can beat an exchange
item.description: A Monero–Bitcoin atomic swap trades coins across two blockchains without a custodian, trading exchange trust for protocol complexity, liquidity limits and slower settlement.

item.title: A Stuck Bridge Can Be a Nonce Problem on the Source Chain
item.description: A pending source-chain transaction can block later sends; learn when a same-nonce replacement helps, when it cannot, and how to clear the queue safely.

item.title: Ripple embeds Privy wallets in XRPL as AI payments top 14 million
item.description: Ripple and Privy are bringing embedded wallets to XRPL as its AI-payment dashboard tops 14 million transactions, widening access while leaving scale and value unresolved.

item.title: Three checks before moving USDC to Arbitrum
item.description: Before bridging USDC to Arbitrum, check the destination chain, token form and route, then keep enough ETH for the transfer and your first transaction.

item.title: A Cross-Chain Swap Quote Is a Route, Not a Promise
item.description: A cross-chain quote is a route proposal, not a guarantee: check token identity, minimum output, fees, gas costs, and delivery conditions before signing.

item.title: Wallet bridges should wait for finality when settlement matters
item.description: A wallet bridge should treat confirmations as a speed signal and finalized blocks as a stronger settlement threshold, with chain and bridge design setting the right wait.

item.title: Network School takes Farcaster, adds user social contract
item.description: Network School has taken Farcaster from Neynar and will condition posting on a new social contract, testing how an open protocol can enforce community rules.
